items.a: **Language.** No chat, no code, no essay, no "you're absolutely right." A true/false for Fable or Astra can wander for **4,000 tokens** and cost **11 cents**. Jev has to come back as a **choice, a score, or a null**.

items.q: Who shipped it, and for how much?
items.a: **Diogo Almeida**, ex-OpenAI instruction-following, two years in stealth. **TypeSafe**, **$40 million**. Host speed: **200× faster**, then **400×** and later **440×** cheaper, output tokens free. Those are his lines.

sections.title: The type is not the truth

items.q: If a type error is impossible, why can it still be wrong?
items.a: The **shape is guaranteed**. The **label is not**. Same question, same context, **different answers**. A null on "is this a horse?" can still ban the wrong account.

items.q: What is a 60% from Jev supposed to mean?
items.a: **RLCD**: a hit rate, not a vibe. 60% means right about **60% of the time**. Chat models are trained to sound sure. The Anchorman line is the joke on top of that claim.

sections.title: The weights might not be the product

items.a: A frozen **Qwen-4B**, **one forward pass**, no new training, a **3090**, plus a **browser demo**. It copies the interface. The CEO has not published the architecture. A paper is maybe.

items.q: Where does this sit next to the Balatro stream?
items.a: This clip is the **pitch and the objection**. Primeagen's stream is the **loop**: typed questions, dirty state, a behavior tree. Menu clicks there. This video never plays the game.
